content:
<<UPDATE>>

small change in statement but maybe an issue with existing codes in arena:
the value 0 is now used for TZAAR and 2 for TOTT.

[type: type of the top piece of the stack (0 = tzaar, 1 = tzarra, 2 = tott)]

All sections
* Consider changing "TZAAR", "TZARRA" and "TOTT" to lowercase and formatting the terms (both singular and plural ones) in italics instead.

Rules
* The phrase "4 rings around an empty center" is a little unclear. Consider replacing it with "there is no playable space in the center".

* Coordinates: It's a bit indirect to describe the axis instead of the coordinates themselves, and the diagram makes some details redundant. Consider rewriting the section as follows:

The board uses an (<var>X</var>, <var>Y</var>) coordinate system with both coordinates ranging from <const>0</const> to <const>8</const>. <var>X</var>-coordinates increase from bottom-left to top-right, and <var>Y</var>-coordinates increase from top to bottom. For easy reference, the coordinates of every space are shown in the initial board setup diagram below.

* Game phases: Please rewrite the note for clarity:
On the first turn of the game, Player <const>0</const> (Red) plays Phase 1 only and skips Phase 2.

* Movement & Capture:
  • Please change "straight lines" to "a straight line" to avoid the impression that a multi-segment path is acceptable.

  • Please mention that pieces cannot move across the center of the board.

  • Capturing: For clarity, please replace the last sentence with: The captured stack is removed, and the attacking stack moves onto the space.

  • Reinforcing: Please add to the end: If this removes your last remaining piece of a type from the board, you immediately lose the game.

Victory Conditions
* Consider removing the second condition, since it's already covered under Defeat Conditions.

Input
* Is it possible to use 0 for TZAAR and 2 for TOTT instead, so that the order of piece types is consistent throughout the statement?

* x, y: Please change "space" to "stack".

Input / Stub
* Consider shortening the variable name "validPieceCount" to "pieceCount".

* Please update the variable names in the stub to be consistent with the Input section.

Output
* Please format x1, y1, x2 and y2 using <var>.

"Initial board setup" in Rules / Viewer
* The pieces used for TZAARs and TZARRAs are swapped compared to the "Non-random starting position" figure on Wikipedia.

Referee
* [EDIT: point removed]

* Consider rewording the defeat messages:
  • missing => no remaining

  • cannot capture => no valid capture available

* I started a game and printed "WAIT". I immediately got eliminated and the console showed:

First action of the turn must be a capture.
Expected output format: 'MOVE q1 r1 q2 r2' or 'WAIT'

Consider rewording to "Phase 1 requires a capture" to avoid the wording "First action". Also, during Phase 1, WAIT isn't a valid command and shouldn't appear in the expected format.

I'll perform some play-testing later. I've also sent you a PM in the forum; please check it out. Thanks.

Here’s TZAAR (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TZAAR), a abstract strategy game designed by Kris Burm for the GIPF Project. 

Have fun! :)

Blimey! I really thought this time the contribution would be perfect – at least the statements! :) I’ve a feeling I’m going to be giving you quite a bit of work (again) with the next ones! :D

Thanks for bringing all these points up! I’m on it!
Haha, no worries at all. I'm always happy to help! 😊

All the corrections have been implemented.:)
Thanks again!

Stub
* Please update the variable names in the stub to be consistent with the Input section.

Output
* Please change "Output" to "Output for one game turn". (The same applies to Brandubh.)

Referee
* In one game, Blue captured Red's last tzarra in Phase 1, but Blue still lost because they didn't output anything in Phase 2. Blue would win only if they completed Phase 2. Please either:

  • Expand the current game phase note to clarify that, after the first turn, victory/defeat is checked only after both phases have been completed, except that an invalid move immediately ends the game; or

  • Change the referee to check for victory/defeat after each phase.

* If the first option above is chosen, please clarify the outcome if a player captures the opponent's last piece of a type in Phase 1 but then eliminates their own last piece of a type through reinforcement in Phase 2. Are they considered the winner or loser?

* In this replay https://www.codingame.com/replay/898518373, Blue reinforced onto its final tzarra. The referee didn't declare Blue the loser in that turn, but instead declared Red the loser in the following turn because it timed out. However, if Red played two more phases, the referee would then declare Blue the loser.

* The referee checks for "PASS", but "PASS" isn't a valid action.

* Please add an error message such as "Non-integer input" when the output contains strings or floating-point values. (The same issue was raised for Quarto, which you've already fixed).

* Error message: Please update 'MOVE q1 r1 q2 r2' to 'MOVE x1 y1 x2 y2'.

* When MOVE has too few parameters (e.g. "MOVE 2"), the console displays the expected output format twice:

Invalid MOVE command format. Expected: MOVE q1 r1 q2 r2
Expected output format: 'MOVE q1 r1 q2 r2'

Consider displaying it once only.

* When I output "MOVE 4 5 4 0 0", the referee appears to ignore the extra parameter and attempts to execute the move. The console shows:

Invalid move from (0,1) to (0,-4)
Expected output format: 'MOVE q1 r1 q2 r2'

Please update the referee to validate the number of parameters before attempting to execute the move.

* As shown in the previous point, there's an issue with the coordinates displayed. It also occurs for other invalid MOVE commands, e.g. moves across the centre. I assume these are internal referee coordinates. Please check that coordinates are reported using the system explained in the statement.

* The console displays "Expected output format" for almost every error, even when it is not relevant. Consider showing it only for output-format errors.

* The Game Summary currently just repeats the output when the action is MOVE. Consider describing the action instead, e.g. [player]'s stack moved from ([x1], [y1]) to ([x2], [y2]) and [captured/reinforced] the stack there. (The same issue occurs in Pentago.)

* Optional: Consider replacing the generic "Invalid MOVE" message with more specific error categories.

Thanks.

Thanks for this new review! :) All points are addressed.

On the phase question, I went with the second option: the referee now checks victory/defeat immediately after each phase, for both players. This makes your follow-up scenario impossible rather than needing a ruling: if a player captures the opponent's last piece of a type in Phase 1, the game ends right there and Phase 2 never happens, so they can't then eliminate their own last piece. That was my main reason for preferring this option over clarifying the statement, the first option would have required an arbitrary decision for that case.

The same root cause explained all three referee issues: the elimination check only ran at the start of the acting player's turn, and only for that player. It now runs after every action, for both.

The statement has also been updated to state explicitly that the game can end mid-turn.

(I’ll sort out Brandubh and Pentago a bit later)
